recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future modernization, such as replacing Command with method or updating the RFC reference beyond RFC 7231, should be handled as a new terminology/editorial decision rather than inferred from FHIR-17092.
issue_request: FHIR-17092 asked to replace terse HTTP verb definitions with fuller definitions that at least point to the HTTP specification, using GET as the example and applying the pattern to other verbs. Jira status is Published with Persuasive resolution, and the only comment says the issue was already fixed.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentions FHIR-17092. The matching application trail is the related FHIR-16078 source work: f4da5602278eaa3576addcf3402cd8cf00b96a98 added an HTTP RFC link to the historical HTTPVerb description and changed bare per-code labels such as HTTP GET into sentence-style definitions such as HTTP GET Command; 86a07e2f5a18780ff44c6ef3daf33f0e6a85f066 updated the link to RFC 7231. Later source refactors carried those definitions into source/bundle/codesystem-http-verb.xml and source/bundle/valueset-http-verb.xml.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini and Bundle.entry.request.method is required-bound to ValueSet/http-verb. Current CodeSystem/http-verb and ValueSet/http-verb source include the HTTP RFC 7231 link, and the CodeSystem contains definitions for GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, and PATCH. Focused Jira searches found FHIR-16078 as the same change family, while Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant FHIR-17092 discussion or conflict. The combined branch already has a FHIR-6109 audit confirming the HTTP verb ValueSet exists.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current source already resolves the issue's implementer-facing concern: it points to the HTTP RFC and no longer uses the original bare labels as definitions. Exact adoption of the Jira example wording would be optional editorial churn rather than a necessary correction.

related_jiras.note: Published issue and source commit that added the HTTP RFC link and improved HTTP verb definitions, explaining FHIR-17092's already-fixed comment.
Earlier HTTP verb ValueSet issue already represented on the combined branch; it confirms the terminology artifact exists but is not the definition-wording decision.
